children: Ryanair Holdings is set to face headwinds from fuel costs in fiscal 2028, but its plans for stock buybacks of 800 million euros could outweigh them, RBC Capital Markets' Ruairi Cullinane says in a research note. The Irish airline group is reviewing all costs given that current forward prices point to a 2 billion-euro increase in fuel costs in fiscal 2028, ahead of consensus expectations of 1 billion euros, according to RBC. While fuel prices are a risk to consensus expectations, the market probably anticipated this risk, the analyst says. Meanwhile, quarterly results that were broadly as expected and a new buyback that represents 3%-4% of Ryanair's market value should be well-received, he adds. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
